what: A 1px line attached to the bottom edge of the header bar signals page turns — on an open page the line fills from the left to the end over 1s sine.inOut, then vanishes .5s later over 1s circ.in. When a link to another page is clicked, the line grows from 0 to 40% over 1s power1.in before navigating. No curtain covers the screen, so the page stays visible during the transition

options.dur: Time in seconds for the line to grow to grow after press, default 1
options.wait: Seconds from the press to navigation, same as the default dur — 0 navigates right away. To navigate before the line finishes growing like the original, keep it short (renewal-brand .28)
options.fill: Length filled in on the opened page (seconds), default 1
options.start: Wait before the fill-up on an opened page (seconds), default 0 — original starts after the app attaches (renewal-brand .1 — original is 0~.22s per page)

use:
…
— For apps that page often: data-fx-nav-progress-line="wait: 0.3"

from.where: 1px line under the shared header and phone menu (Next transition — on leaving, width 0→40% 1s power1.in starts and the new page arrives at .52s, on arrival 100% 1s sine.inOut · opacity 0 1s delayed .5s circ.in) · wait: 0.28 (local navigation takes .27s so the screen changes at .55s) · start: 0.1 (when Next attaches, 0 to .22s per page)

note: The original moves on as soon as the Next router receives the new page (.52s), while the line grows toward 40% over 1s in the meantime. This Motion part is a normal transition: it grows the line, moves on after the wait seconds, and the opened page fills again from 0. A line inside a hidden header (display:none) receives no press, so even if it is attached to both the wide-screen header and the phone header, it advances only once.
